points.title: What a data dictionary is
points.must: A document or table that describes the structure of a database — data about the data (metadata); for every table it lists every field.

points.title: Data and metadata
points.must: Metadata is data that describes other data, with an example: 14/03/2009 is data; 'DateOfBirth, Date, DD/MM/YYYY, required' is metadata.

points.title: What it records for each field
points.must: At least five of: field name, data type, size, format, key (PK/FK), validation rule, required / null, description, example.

points.title: An example entry
points.must: One field described in full, e.g. DateOfBirth — Date — 10 — DD/MM/YYYY — PK/none — validation range — example value.

points.title: Data types
points.must: Text / VARCHAR(n), CHAR(n), Integer, Real / Decimal, Date / Time, Boolean, each with an example field or value.

points.title: Phone numbers as text
points.must: A phone number is stored as Text: it can start with + or 0, has spaces and no arithmetic is done with it.

points.title: Naming fields
points.must: No spaces, meaningful names, one style, the same name for the same data in every table (e.g. StudentID in Students and Loans).

points.title: When it is written
points.must: During the design stage of the system life cycle, after the ERD and before the database is built; kept up to date while the system is used.

points.title: Purpose: one agreed definition and consistency
points.must: Everyone uses the same names and types; the same field has the same type and size in every table, so primary and foreign keys match.

points.title: Other purposes and users
points.must: Helps programmers build the database and write SQL; records validation rules (data integrity); helps testers and maintenance / new developers.

points.title: What goes wrong without it
points.must: An example of problems: a key is Text in one table and Integer in another so tables cannot be joined; dates in different formats; invalid data accepted.

points.title: Active and passive data dictionaries
points.must: Active: kept by the DBMS, updated automatically (system catalogue, e.g. information_schema); passive: a document kept by people, updated by hand, may become out of date.

points.title: ERD, data dictionary and database
points.must: ERD shows entities and relationships; the data dictionary describes every field; the database holds the real records.
